### [Acrostic Poem at the Bottom]

Censure not the Books OF THIS man, I say to you, SOPHIST:
Oh, let your work yield to the AMPHITHEATER of Heinrich!
For by the instinct of the Sacred Divinity, he has duly performed [his work];
Truly these Writings are never contrary to TRUTH;
Because he defends and adorns a Sincere WISDOM,
And also restores [wisdom], purging and illuminating its misuse.
In life, he wanted to serve GOD and the Deity,
So that, with equal reason, the Name and Omen of KHUNRATH,
GREAT IN COUNSEL, would celebrate the Gifts of JEHOVAH.
Finally, nothing remains but for him to despise the Jests of Momus;
And THUS, by writing, may he continue to benefit many:
Since he excels in talent and is refined by Art.

**[Signature to the right of the poem:]**
M. Andr.
Ricciius.

### [Notes on the Landscape]

The engraving illustrates the concepts within the text. The waterfall and the rising mist represent the "ascent and descent" of the spirit mentioned in the final lines, while the massive rock itself signifies the "Earth" which acts as the nurse and stabilizer for these divine energies. The figures at the base of the rock appear to be contemplatives or seekers, studying the "secrets" revealed in the landscape.

<summary>This page translates the Latin inscription on the monumental rock, revealing it to be the Emerald Tablet of Hermes Trismegistus, a central text of alchemical philosophy. The text outlines the principle of "as above, so below" and the creation of the world from a single source.</summary>
<keywords>Emerald Tablet, Hermes Trismegistus, alchemy, hermeticism, Tabula Smaragdina, as above so below, macrocosm, microcosm</keywords>

# Landscape of the Great Work

### Description of the Illustration
<note>This etching depicts the "Alchemical Landscape," a common motif where the search for the Philosopher's Stone is visualized as a physical journey through nature.</note>

This page features a large, detailed landscape etching. 

*   **Left side:** A rocky path leads upward past a small building or shrine. A figure, possibly a traveler or a shepherd <note>Representing the alchemist or the "seeker" of wisdom</note>, is visible on the path.
*   **Right side:** A large, craggy rock formation dominates the middle ground, representing the "Earth" and the raw material of the work.
*   **Foreground:** A body of water—possibly a pond or river—is filled with reeds and what appear to be swans or water birds <note>In alchemy, the swan often symbolizes the "White Stage" or Albedo, a process of purification.</note>.
*   **Background:** Sparse trees and distant hills are visible, suggesting the vastness of the natural world.

<meta>This page serves as the formal entrance or "Gate" to Khunrath’s work. It transitions from the previous page's metaphorical landscape into a specific, programmatic explanation of his "Theo-magical" philosophy, where the study of nature is treated as a divine school.</meta>

[Top Left, within the ray of light]
-> **LORD** <note>Hebrew: יהוה (the Tetragrammaton, the name of God)</note> <-
-> **LIGHT WITH DIVINITY AND** <-
-> **DIVINITY IN LIGHT.** <note>original: "CVM NVMINE LVMEN ET IN LVMINE NVMEN"</note> <-

[Top Right, title]
# THE GATE
## OF THE AMPHITHEATER
### OF ETERNAL WISDOM,
### THE ONLY TRUE ONE.

[Labels within the landscape]
(Top right peaks): **EVERYTHING MOVES IN HARMONY** <note>Greek: ΠΑΝΤΑ ΑΙΣΟΝ ΚΙΝΕΙ</note>
(Left cave entrance): **HOLY SPIRIT** <note>original: SPIRITVS SANCTVS</note>
(Central cave/structure): **PRAYER** <note>original: ORATIO</note>
(Central stone tablet):
**BE**
**ONE**
**IN EVERY**
**THING**
**BEWARE**
**LEST**
**YOU BE ALONE** <note>original Latin: "VNVS ESTO IN OMNI RE CAVE NE SOLVS"</note>

[Bottom Text Block]
A SKETCH of that Theo-magical, macro-cosmic, and universal SCHOOL <term>Gymnasium: Here meaning a place of rigorous training for both the mind and soul</term>, which is the public and great **all-encompassing circle** <note>Greek: ἐγκύκλιον (enkyklion)</note> of NATURE, liberally built by JEHOVAH ELOHIM <note>A Hebrew name for God used here to emphasize His role as Creator of the physical world</note> for all, for everyone, for each and every individual. Here, through the Heaven, Stars, Earth, Sea, Waters, Stones, Plants, Animals, Minerals and Metals; indeed, through all things which are born either in the womb of the Sea, or in the belly or surface of the Earth, or under the Heaven—the wondrous JEHOVAH has written his marvelous WISDOM in the great and universal book of Nature. This book was made by the finger of the Omnipotent God, and in it, the Divinity and Light of NATURE, essentially and really existing, a wise spark of eternal WISDOM, tirelessly teaches and professes by manifesting through natural magic. 

The Fathers and Ancestors—those faithful teachers of faithful sons, the ancient Magi or Sages and Philosophers (for whom the World served as books, its Parts and Regions as pages, and its innumerable fruits as letters and Languages)—frequented this school long ago throughout its length, breadth, height, and depth. They were **admirers of the great "World-book of Nature," extremely deep and widely learned** <note>original German: "abs hoch-stieff und weit-gelehrt des grossen, Weltbuchs der Natur admiratores"</note>, who studied it with diverse industry. Even today, all faithful students of Theosophical <term>Theosophy: "God-wisdom," a blend of mystical insight and natural philosophy</term> philosophy—the only true kind—are not ashamed to visit it faithfully (and not in vain!) by Divine authority and the wise example of the Sages. 

Thus, surely, by the Grace of GOD, inspired and illuminated from heaven by the Divinity and Light of ELOHIM, they might explain these things—partly through the "Signatures" or divine hieroglyphic characters of Nature, by which things themselves speak **Kabbalistically** <note>referring to Kabbalah, the Jewish mystical tradition of finding hidden meanings in symbols and letters</note> with men and are made equal to them. Partly, indeed, through the most sagacious **Vulcanic Anatomy** <term>Anatomiâ Vulcanicâ: "Chemistry through fire." Vulcan was the god of the forge; here it refers to alchemical laboratory work</term>, they might draw a solid and perfect knowledge of ETERNAL WISDOM, which is wisely manifested in this Universal World. There, as if from the clearest fountain of philosophy, while **Praying and Working** <note>original: "Orantes & Laborantes," the core alchemical motto</note> with mind, reason, and senses, they might become genuine Physicists and true Philosophers—not merely guessing, but knowing. 

Many have been made so; they are being made; they will be made. For by this orthodox and truly Theosophical method of philosophizing, we are able to see and know—physically and philosophically—from the Creature (as if from a bright and clear mirror of Nature) the CREATOR (specifically His eternal Power and Divinity, as in Romans 1:20), and JESUS CHRIST whom He sent, and OURSELVES. We also see the inexhaustible treasures of the Divinity and Light of NATURE. From these, we learn to philosophize wisely and correctly, always and everywhere; we learn to live well, and to die blessedly. This is impossible for the **one-eyed Sophists** <note>A derogatory term for academics who rely only on logic and book-learning, lacking spiritual "vision."</note>. This is the peak of Sincere Philosophy! Fie on the slanderer! 

Invented by HEINRICH KHVNRATH OF LEIPZIG, faithful lover of Theosophy, and Doctor of both Medicines. In the year 1602 since the MESSIAH <note>original: "MASCHIACH"</note> was sent.

[Bottom Right Box]
E P <note>Likely the initials of the engraver</note>

[Right Margin, handwritten note]
20
<unclear>Reading</unclear>

<summary>This title page functions as a theological and scientific manifesto, presenting the "Book of Nature" as a divine classroom where the seeker uses both prayer and alchemical fire (Vulcanic Anatomy) to find God. It establishes Khunrath’s "Theo-magical" approach, which insists that true science cannot be separated from spiritual devotion.</summary>
<keywords>Heinrich Khunrath, Theosophy, Book of Nature, Vulcanic Anatomy, Alchemy, Signatures, Kabbalah, Elohim, Ora et Labora, 1602</keywords>

# TO THE
# SINCERE READER,
# GREETINGS.

[Large decorative initial A] SINCERE AND FRIENDLY READER, we now give to you, in its entirety and completed, this REMARKABLE WORK OF THE AMPHITHEATER. In it, the author Heinrich Khunrath of Leipzig, Doctor of both Medicine and Philosophy, has set forth for all people—with admirable industry—**DIVINE, HUMAN, MACRO- AND MICROCOSMIC WISDOM** <note>Macrocosm refers to the universe as a whole, while Microcosm refers to the human being as a reflection of that universe.</note>: Divine-Magical, Christian-Kabbalistic, and Physio-Chemical, to be viewed with the **EYES**, contemplated with the **MIND**, and pursued by **Work**, in the Oratory and Laboratory <note>original: *in Oratorio & Laboratorio*. This is Khunrath’s famous motto, suggesting that spiritual insight (prayer/meditation) must be combined with practical alchemical work.</note>. The author himself, prevented by an untimely death, left the work behind him incomplete in some parts, though not significantly so. As he was dying, he placed that burden upon my shoulders—which are indeed unequal to the task—so that this posthumous **WORK** might be brought to light through my care. This was done both because I was joined to him in close friendship, and because he made me a participant in his plan for publishing this work, along with other more secret things he left behind.

I have therefore applied myself diligently so that it might come forth to the public just as I accurately understood he himself wished it to appear. If it does not satisfy everyone in every respect, let them weigh the magnitude of the **MATTER** and let them produce better things than these.

It remains for me to advise you briefly about the purpose of the Work: It is admitted by all how naturally the human mind desires **TO KNOW**, and with what great care it does so. How many volumes of books are unrolled for the sake of the Sciences? How many troubles are endured? How many expenses are paid out, and how many nighttime studies, vigils, and labors are exhausted? The end of all these is often at last either vanity or poverty, and frequently even the broken strength of the body and madness of the mind; to such an extent does human reason show a difficult path and approach to "shadowy philosophy" <note>original: *Philosophiam umbratilem*. Likely referring to speculative or academic philosophy that lacks the light of divine revelation.</note>. 

Our **THEOSOPHY** <note>Divine Wisdom</note> in this **WORK** acts quite differently; for first, it does not consist of so many labors and expenses. Hear Wisdom Herself speaking to you: *She is easily seen by those who love her, and found by those who seek her:*

<margin>Wisdom of Solomon 6, verse 13.</margin>

10
She <note>Wisdom is personified as a female figure in the biblical and alchemical traditions.</note> anticipates those who desire her, so that she might show herself to them first. He who watches for her from daybreak shall not labor, for he shall find her **SITTING** at his doors. Furthermore, she is not occupied with so many troubles. For her conversation has no bitterness, nor her company any weariness, but rather gladness and joy. Therefore, this Wisdom of ours is most easy and spontaneous. Such are all the **TRUE GIFTS OF GOD**. But the frauds of the world, illusions, fantasies, and the sophistry of the Devil, cost much labor and expense.

Finally, you must be discouraged from despising this Work; it is the mark of a foolish and inept man to judge a thing not yet read, and to despise what is not understood. I ask you, are the stars to be despised because you do not recognize them? Or are the plants which fertile Mother Earth offers us to be cast away and trampled underfoot because you do not perceive their <term>signature</term> <note>The "Doctrine of Signatures" was the belief that plants' physical appearances revealed their medicinal or spiritual uses.</note> and hidden powers? How many useless and fatuous offspring does human wit give birth to? And yet, you often give them the primary place in your library, and they have the first seats at your philosophical table. Remember, therefore, that this **AMPHITHEATER** does not propose to your eyes a painted or fatuous philosophy to behold, but the contemplation of **THE ONLY TRUE ETERNAL WISDOM**, which you would neglect and despise to your great harm and destruction. **FAREWELL**, and enjoy this Amphitheater, for the acknowledgment of **GOD**, the knowledge of yourself, the discerning of Nature, for the illumination of the Soul, the purity of the Spirit, and the health of the Body.

Given at Wernigerode in the famous County of Stolberg at the <term>Bructerus</term> <note>The Brocken mountain in the Harz range, legendary for its association with alchemy and folklore.</note> on the Ides of March, in the year of the health-bringing Virgin Birth 1609.

**ERASMUS WOLFART.** <note>Wolfart was the physician and friend of Khunrath who oversaw this posthumous edition.</note>

A POEM OF PRAISE
BY THEOPHILUS ARETIUS <note>A pseudonym meaning "lover of virtue."</note>
CONCERNING THAT GREAT AND WONDROUS **AMPHITHEATER**
OF THE MOST ILLUSTRIOUS GENTLEMAN, LORD
**HEINRICH KHUNRATH OF LEIPZIG**,
DOCTOR OF BOTH MEDICINES <note>While usually referring to Canon and Civil Law, in Khunrath's alchemical context, "Both Medicines" refers to the healing of the physical body and the "medicine" of the soul or base metals.</note>, AND RESTORER
OF TRUE **WISDOM** AND THE STUDY THEREOF.

[Decorative initial A] If anyone should look more deeply into the hidden mysteries of the divine Word, and hide himself within its innermost sanctuaries, he will see nothing but the commerce of men with the heavenly beings. Happy are the souls whom such great grace has blessed—to hear angelic tongues while still in a mortal body, and to feel the voice of **GOD** within a human breast! Where has that day fled? Where now is the golden ladder of heaven hidden, by which the celestial beings descend? Or who shall unlock the sacred entrances and lead us to the holy Divinities?

Believe me, he who attempts such things enters upon a difficult path; for the Divinities dwelling in the starry lights of the gods are not manifest to everyone. Yet, if we believe that angelic minds once delighted in human companionship, I believe there is an abstruse art: the ancient Fathers knew it. It has set: just as the Sun is submerged in the deep Ocean, soon shapeless darkness and incurable error prevailed; and the liar raised its head from the underworld <note>original: "orco," referring to the abyss or the realm of the dead.</note>.

There is a pure fountain of **WISDOM**: the divine <term>Kabbalah</term> <note>A mystical Jewish tradition that Khunrath integrated into his "Christian Kabbalah," seeking hidden meanings in scripture.</note>, and that which the **MAGI** possess—the Sabaeans <note>An ancient people of South Arabia, legendary for their wealth and their trade in frankincense and perfumes.</note> smelling of incense—and to which he gave the name **GREEN**, and the silent, molten **SALT** <note>These are alchemical references; "Green" often refers to the "Green Lion" or the vitriol of the wise, and "Salt" is one of the three primary principles of matter.</note>. No one shall possess this threefold Wisdom of **GOD** without divine inspiration: the Theological, the Astronomical, and the Healing Diana <note>Diana, the goddess of the moon, here represents the medicinal or silver-related aspect of alchemy.</note>; no one is great and exalted without divine breath. This threefold Wisdom flows from a single blessed fountain of the ethereal Spirit, and from the Mind poured through all things, which gives life to the lands and fills the sea, the stars, and the air. The King of Peace <note>A reference to King Solomon, who was traditionally granted supreme wisdom and command over spirits by God.</note> shall be my witness, who once held as many gems of Wisdom in his breast as there are sands upon the shores, in whose heart Wisdom had built a high citadel.

How often, repeating sighs from his deepest heart, had he called the beautiful dove from the mountain of Lebanon? <note>A reference to the Song of Solomon, interpreted here as the soul seeking Wisdom.</note> For he had chosen for himself a single companion for life. "O my beloved, come," prays your dearest spouse, the King of Jerusalem <note>original: "Rex Solymæ"</note>; and the sacred Divinities swear that he will be a constant and chaste husband to you.

Abraham, relying on the present conversations of **JEHOVAH**, was skilled in this Wisdom; setting out from the Chaldean people, he brought it to Egypt and revealed it to the lands of Idumea.

By this knowledge of things, Jacob, it was known to you; to you appeared **JEHOVAH**, and to you the Ladder of **GOD**; the palace of the open sky was seen; you filled the flock with spotted offspring. <note>Refers to Jacob's use of "magic" rods to influence the breeding of Laban’s livestock in Genesis 30.</note>

The son of Rachel: <note>Joseph.</note> while the court of the Egyptian <note>original: "Pharii"</note> king holds him, he carefully interprets dreams; wise regarding the future, the seer sings of things to come through mystical cups.

Moses, brought up in the Egyptian court, drank this in; by this, and then flashing with divine light (a double light), he was able to present himself before **JEHOVAH** himself.

By this, Balaam—while still sincere and free from the crime of base greed—knew how to properly search the hidden things of the high **GOD** and to bless the holy people.

By this, the clever Queen of the Arabs <note>The Queen of Sheba.</note> brought riddles to the King of the Israelites <note>original: "Isacidum," referring to Solomon.</note>, than whom no other shone more wise. By this Daniel, more excellent than the Magi, was brought forth by the Royal school of Persia; he declared the saddest fates to two kings: one falls from power, while the other becomes like a beast. <note>Belshazzar and Nebuchadnezzar.</note>

How great a name did Hermes Trismegistus <note>original: "ter maximus Hermes," the legendary founder of alchemy and hermeticism.</note> carry because of this? By this, having worshipped **GOD**, she <note>Likely referring to the Sibyls or divine Wisdom herself.</note> visited the cradle of **CHRIST**. Reuchlin <note>Johannes Reuchlin (1455–1522), a German humanist who integrated Kabbalah into Christian thought.</note> taught the same through the wondrous **WORD**.

The wise Agrippa <note>Heinrich Cornelius Agrippa (1486–1535), author of *Three Books of Occult Philosophy*.</note> brought this forth with a wondrous mouth. The Swiss Hermes <note>A reference to Paracelsus (1493–1541), the famous Swiss physician and alchemist.</note>, son of the Muses, brought it forth—he who is hated by fools, but is a vast Light to the Wise, and whose Wisdom exceeds human senses. Rejoice, Germany, in this lofty Apollo. Stellatus <note>Marcello Palingenio Stellato, author of the *Zodiacus Vitae*.</note> also preserves this in honeyed song.

This is, believe me, this is that Science which truly spreads before you the Light of Nature and the hidden forces of the vast world. It is the brightest Light, without which all things lie submerged in deep darkness. This is your torch; this Light, this guide going before you, will lead you suddenly to the hidden inner sanctuaries of all things.

And thus, you will be no empty weight in this wondrous Theater, nor a passive spectator; but you will be a Searcher, a Doer, and an intimate guest—not a guest always wandering outside.

By this he reveals the courses and powers of the stars, and having examined their changes, marks the true, fixed times.

This power envelops the force of the winds and the surges of the Sea;

### EPIGRAMMA

### ON THE EDITION OF THE 
### **AMPHITHEATRE** OF THE ILLUSTRIOUS 
### MAN, LORD HEINRICH KHVNRATH OF LEIPZIG, 
### DOCTOR OF BOTH MEDICINES <note>original: "Vtriusque Medicinae." This likely refers to Khunrath’s mastery of both traditional physical medicine and "spagyric" or alchemical medicine.</note>, DISTINGUISHED 
### PHILOSOPHER, AND THE FOREMOST 
### OF OUR AGE, ETC., 
### FOR HIS HONORED PATRON.

YOU who enjoy finding fault, seek to find no fault here;
Let all labor yield to this physical **Amphitheatre**.
Which Khunrath—through love of the truth,
And by the inspiration of the Divine—has prepared,
Drawn forth by the **HIGHEST PHYSICIAN** <note>Referring to God as the ultimate healer.</note> from the 
Lofty sense; he illuminates the sacred uses of Wisdom,
Restores what has fallen, and cleanses the diseased limbs.
In the World, there is no one equal to him in these virtues;
As "the lion is known by its claw," <note>original: "Vngue leo notus." A Latin proverb meaning a great artist or thinker can be recognized by even a small sample of their work.</note> he is known by this Divine art.
From which the greatest glory shall be born as these books are spread;
God’s gifts vary, and this is certainly a noble gift.
From a hundred thousand men, or even more, 
Scarcely one is fortunate enough to possess such genius.

*M. ZVBERVS, Poet Laureate*

### THEOSOPHICAL PRAYER
### TO
### THE FOUNTAIN OF WISDOM
### CHRIST, THE BEST
### AND GREATEST.
By a Heart-felt Christian. <note>original: "Christiani Cordati"</note>

**C**HRIST, make me wise, for You alone are the **WISDOM** of the Father, and whoever is wise with You is truly wise. For in such great darkness, who will give me light so that I might grasp the sweet path of true salvation? I flee to You, who are the very **LIGHT** for mortals, through whom all created things have perceived the day. Grant me the **LIGHT OF NATURE** <term>Lumen Naturae: a central concept in Christian Theosophy and Alchemy referring to the divine spark of intelligence within the natural world that allows the human mind to understand the secrets of creation</term>, and drive back the darkness; let Your Spirit illuminate my heart.

Indeed, I confess I am not worthy of such great honor; I am a wretch, O Christ, and guilty of many a sin. Yet I trust in Your shed blood, of which a tiny drop shall purge my filth. If You give me life, why would You not also, out of Your goodness, grant us all life’s necessities? For You say that whatever we ask of the Father in Your name, we shall surely receive.

I seek no profit for myself, nor do I claim vain praise; You alone shall be my praise and my prize. Do not grant me riches for a greedy man to admire; all such things fail, for the world holds no lasting wealth. Breathe upon my endeavors; fill my mind with celestial fires, and take away the heavy shadows from my art <note>The "art" here likely refers to the "Sacred Art" of theosophy or alchemy, the study of God's signatures in nature</note>. Nothing shall be obscure; I shall be led easily into the inner sanctuaries of Nature, if You, O Christ, show me the way. I myself shall bring You great thanks as the rewards of my praise; for man has nothing greater that he can return to You.

### PROLOGUE

<summary>This page acts as the formal frontispiece for the prologue of Heinrich Khunrath's major work, establishing its interdisciplinary nature as a blend of Kabbalah, magic, and alchemy. It serves as a universal invitation to all seekers to enter the "Amphitheatre of Eternal Wisdom."</summary>

<meta>Page 18 established the universal scope of the work. Page 19 now details the structure and spiritual methodology of the "Prologue," describing it as a seven-step ladder toward divine wisdom and the Philosopher's Stone.</meta>

19

[Decorative header with floral and geometric patterns]

**T**his present **PROLOGUE** is likened to a certain **LADDER** of **SEVEN** mystical and orthodox **STEPS**, intended for the **STUDIES** of true **WISDOM** and the method of right **PHILOSOPHY**. By this ladder—with **GOD** calling and leading, the **GUARDIAN SPIRIT** <note>original: "GENIO"</note> stimulating, the natural **WIT** <note>original: "INGENIO"</note> cooperating, and diligent **LABOR** performing its duty—a **THEOSOPHIC** ascent is made. This ascent follows the doctrine of true **WISDOM** as well as that of her truly Wise Herald <note>The "Herald" likely refers to King Solomon, often cited by Khunrath as the supreme human authority on Wisdom.</note> (who is most highly approved by **JEHOVAH’S** own reckoning), leading toward the **GATE** of the aforementioned **AMPHITHEATRE**. Although this gate is narrow, small, and despised, it is nevertheless sufficiently majestic and grand: **IN** and **THROUGH** which any faithful son of **DOCTRINE**, persevering constantly until the end, shall joyfully **ENTER**.

There, he shall happily **ATTAIN** that most universal and triune **SUPREME GOOD**, namely: **first**, the Recognition of **GOD** and of Him whom He sent, **JESUS CHRIST**, and the genuine understanding of the Book of Holy Scripture; **second**, the knowledge of **HIMSELF**; **third**, the knowledge of the **Macrocosm** <note>original: "MVNDI maioris" (the greater world/universe)</note> and of its **SON** which He gave—the **MAGNESIA** of the Philosophers. This is the **STONE** of the Philosophers, indeed the universal or more-than-perfect proper and perfect **SUBJECT**, to be made more-than-perfect through Physical Regeneration with the aid of the Chemical Art.

This attainment occurs: **first**, **IN** and **FROM GOD**, and Him whom He sent, **JESUS CHRIST**, and the Book of Holy Scripture; **second**, in and from **HIMSELF**; and **finally third**, in and from the **Macrocosm** and its **SON** which He gave—the **MAGNESIA** of the Wise, **ALL** in **ALL**. (For this reason, man was composed by the Triune **ELOHIM** <note>original Hebrew: אלהים (God)</note> as likewise triune—of Body, Spirit, and Soul—and was placed especially in this worldly Paradise). He shall enjoy this as a certain singular treasure and prize <note>original Greek: "κειμηλίῳ καὶ βραβείῳ" (keimelio kai brabeio)</note> in a theosophic manner.

Moreover, this **PROLOGUE** consists of as many **VERSES** as there are days in the **Year**—namely, three hundred and sixty-five. The purpose is so that throughout the whole year, every single day, **ONE** verse must be most sharply weighed in the balance of accurate contemplation by the genuine student of **WISDOM**, considered with an industrious mind, and frequently examined. In this way, the soul-saving food of this **THEOSOPHIC DOCTRINE** may be more suitably and happily converted for him into a sweet recreation of the Soul and a most effective nourishment of the Mind.

And so also, within the space of a whole year—for it is not the labor or study of one day, or a week, or a month, especially for the recently initiated (believe one who is truthful and taught by **Experience**!)—and indeed with the help and assistance of the **SPIRIT OF THE WISDOM OF GOD** <note>original Hebrew/Latin: "RVACH CHOCHMAH-EL, seu SPIRITVS SAPIENTIÆ DEI"</note> sent by the Father of **LIGHTS**, he may be able not merely to taste superficially or with just the tips of his lips, but, by swallowing deeply and frequently, to taste again and truly—nay, **QUINTESSENTIALLY**—perceive **WHAT**, of what **KIND**, how **GREAT**, and how **SWEET** both true **WISDOM** is, and this method of sincere **PHILOSOPHY**: and what, finally, its **DOCTRINE** cherishes in its innermost retreat.

But these most sumptuously prepared and elegant—nay, **THEOSOPHIC**—feasts, no one will easily taste worthily, much less will they...

THE FIRST STEP is to eagerly and willingly (*quickly and gladly / with delight and joy* <note>original German: "schnell vnd gerne/mit luſt vnd frewden"</note>) Hear the Wise man, as a true and perfect *Theosopher*, a magnificent and Royal herald of the ETERNAL and only true WISDOM, divinely appointed and delegated; and also to hear that aforementioned WISDOM herself. They faithfully call and diligently invite all *Men*—everyone, each and every one—from a singular burning affection of benevolence toward the human race, first to themselves, and then to the Love, Admiration, and study of MAGIC (SOPHIA) <note>Greek: ΜΑΓΕΙΑΣ (ΣΟΦΙΑΣ). and by the giving of oneself, to love her with a thoroughly internal reason; and to ardently continue this study of Her. But as for that wisdom which is human, **carnal** <margin>b Romans 8:7. 2 Corinthians 2:12.</margin>, **worldly** <margin>c 1 Corinthians 1:20 and 1 Corinthians 3:19.</margin>, counterfeited, and supposed—or as if it were some such Wisdom—in **lofty speeches and sophistical and persuasive words** <margin>d 1 Corinthians 2:1 and 4.</margin>, or in the **skill of speaking** <margin>e 1 Corinthians 1:17.</margin>, that is, swollen with the painted colors of the oratorical faculty and ambitious eloquence (from which, by Divine command, the Apostle **PAUL** faithfully warns us); a wisdom proud in its rivalry with **DIVINE** and true **WISDOM**, and superciliously extolling itself, and **deceiving with the probability of speech through false reasoning** <margin>f Colossians 2:4.</margin>; a wisdom diabolically born and most perniciously spread and published through its admirers, who are its own instruments (like unto itself); a wisdom that is spurious and illegitimate, indeed profane, the mother of darkness, vices, errors, seduction, and all confusion, and of that **false philosophy** (named **empty fallacy or deception** <margin>h Colossians 2:8.</margin> by that **chosen vessel of the LORD** <margin>g Acts 9:15. 2 Corinthians 12:1 and 4.</margin>, who was a witness to the third heaven and the mysteries of Paradise)—this false wisdom, true **WISDOM** herself and her Royal herald here depict in her true colors (just as at other times they depict her as **refuse** <note>original Greek: σκύβαλα (*skubala*), a term used by St. Paul meaning dung or worthless filth</note> fit only for swine). One must utterly leave this behind, putting the greatest possible distance between it and oneself; one must hate it worse than (as the saying goes) **a dog or a snake**; indeed, one must severely abominate, execrate, and detest it to one's very last breath. Furthermore, one should, with tireless diligence, call others away and discourage them from its cult as much as possible, lest they embrace or follow it even in the slightest; so that they may begin to hate in good time that which they must flee now and forever.

### ARGUMENT
### OF THE THIRD STEP.

THE THIRD STEP is, by the grace of **JEHOVAH**, to understand and know: What, of what sort, how Beautiful, Noble, and Excellent, and how Great a Thing is **ETERNAL WISDOM**, the only true one? She is the only root, foundation, and the unique, sole, universal, and eternal beginning of a purer, healthier, and truer philosophy—indeed, of the whole of **THEOSOPHY** <note>literally "Divine Wisdom" or "God-Knowledge"</note> and the method of philosophizing correctly. To this is also added: what properly is the aforementioned true **PHILOSOPHY**?

[Decorative horizontal band with floral and scroll motifs]

### ARGUMENT
### OF THE FOURTH STEP.

THE FOURTH STEP is to know who gives true **WISDOM**; with which Teacher or Master, or where she is to be sought and found; from whence she comes; in which Books she is handed down; and in how many ways she has manifested herself from the beginning to all creatures, especially to **Men**. <margin>O what a distinguished offspring indeed! <note>This marginal note refers sarcastically to the "false philosophy" mentioned earlier in the text.</note></margin> And how even today, she offers herself to be seen everywhere innumerably, both in the **Macrocosm** <term>Macrocosm: the Great World or the Universe</term> and the **Microcosm** <term>Microcosm: the Little World, referring to the Human Being as a reflection of the universe</term>, just as she evidently appears in the sacred **BIBLE** (especially to those who are truly illuminated by the rays of the **DIVINE SPIRIT of WISDOM** through a non-feigned **Enthusiasm** <note>In this context, "Enthusiasm" refers to being "filled with God" or divine inspiration rather than mere excitement</note>).

C 3

<summary>This page defines the Third and Fourth Steps of the spiritual ladder, contrasting true Divine Wisdom with "carnal" worldly philosophy and directing the seeker toward the Bible and the study of the Universe (Macrocosm and Microcosm) as the sources of truth.</summary>

[Decorative border]

->ARGUMENT OF THE FIFTH STEP.<-

THE FIFTH STEP is to know to whom true WISDOM is given, and to whom it is not: Who is her genuine, legitimate, and faithful foster-child <note>original: *alumnus*</note>, namely the **Theosopher** <term>A "Theosopher" (Theosophus) in this 16th-century context is one who seeks "God-wisdom," combining deep religious devotion with the study of nature.</term> and the orthodox Philosopher: Who is a **Sophist** <term>A "Sophist" here refers to a false teacher who uses clever but empty or deceptive logic, prioritizing worldly reputation over divine truth.</term>: How, or by what study, or by what method she is to be sought: How she comes and is communicated: By what aids or means; When and in how many ways (with **JEHOVAH** fostering and nodding His assent) she wishes, ought, is able, or can be obtained and perceived: Whether, and What, finally, concerning the more sublime Secrets of this more sincere and Divinely attained Philosophy; by Whom; to Whom; Why, or for what grave causes; How much; under what Laws or Conditions; In what manner; In what places and When, without danger, it should or should Not be set forth, spoken, taught, revealed, and further communicated?

[Decorative border]

->ARGUMENT OF THE SIXTH STEP.<-

THE SIXTH STEP is to know what are the Goods and Gifts of true WISDOM, and, what are the Exercises of the study of Wisdom, that is, of true Philosophy: What is the Use, Abuse, Fruit, and End: and what great and varied Treasures come certainly from there to the sons of Doctrine, most nearly and according to the will of **JEHOVAH**.

[Decorative border]

->ARGUMENT OF THE SEVENTH AND FINAL STEP.<-

<margin>Certainly the end of all Sophists, on account of their contempt for truth, will be tragic; if not in this life, surely in the final judgment: to which all those appeal who see violence being done to the truth, and who are oppressed because of it.</margin>

THE SEVENTH and final Step is NOT to care a whit <note>original: *negry morari*, a Latinized Greek idiom meaning to not value even the grunt of a pig or the smallest trifle</note> for any Sophists, of whatever grain or ilk they may be, who love vanity and seek after lies—<note>The author provides a German translation of the preceding Latin: *Die das Eitele so lieb haben / vnd die Lügen so gerne.*</note>—and those who calumniously bite at the **TRUTH**; indeed, those who frivolously scorn and condemn the only true **WISDOM**, and thus also this only right method or **Theosophic** and orthodox way of philosophizing born from her, namely this **AMPHITHEATER OF ETERNAL WISDOM**, as well as its faithful lovers and followers, the pious searchers of **TRUTH** and **WISDOM**. Rather, it is to value all those [sophists] as nothing, with a great and truly philosophical soul, and in turn to fearlessly estimate them as not worth a single breath; and to eagerly prepare and fully compose oneself for the confession and philosophical defense of the recognized **TRUTH** (according to the grace given to each by **GOD**); and thus finally to propagate it usefully to posterity; and to communicate it to them as is due: indeed, to rejoice with thanksgiving that one is no longer a labyrinthine, one-eyed, and blinking <note>original: *caecutiens*, squinting or half-blind</note> sophist of "opinion," but (one who is ruled by **ETERNAL WISDOM** and **TRUTH**) walks upon the straight line of Truth without any deviation, existing as a true and knowing **PHILOSOPHER**: and so, at last, to please very few, and only those who are **Theosophically** learned, who alone see and know the universal truth. Which, surely, is a sign of **TRUTH** that must not be despised.

I. STEP

### The EXPLANATIONS of the Prologue follow.

**HEAR**] With the ears of reason, intellect, and mind, as much as those of the senses or body: lest you be found in the number of those who have ears and hear not, eyes and see not, whom the blind, malicious pride of the prince of this unclean World has made deaf, mute, and blind. **Son**] "Son" is the same to the Hebrews as "MAN" or "MALE" is to the Latins: hence, since the wise King addresses everyone, he uses this universal term. For **WISDOM** calls to all, Proverbs 8, verse 4, and 9:4. This Wisdom, having become incarnate, says: *Come to me all you who labor and are burdened: I will refresh you.* <note>original: *κατ' ἐξοχὴν* (kat' exochēn)</note>—that is, by way of excellence—"Son" is understood as the faithful and beloved heir of **DOCTRINE**, **DISCIPLINE**, and **ETERNAL WISDOM**. **Magnificent herald**] Because he is a King, the son of a King, and illuminated, taught, and led by **JEHOVAH HIMSELF**, by the **DIVINE SPIRIT OF WISDOM**, (1 Kings 3). He is most greatly to be believed as one who is experienced, and also wisely chosen and appointed for this use by **SUPER-CELESTIAL SOPHIA** <note>Sophia is the Greek word for Wisdom, personified here as a divine guide.</note>. **To know WISDOM, etc.**] All these things, of which an enumeration is made in this place, are Good and...

4 INTERPRETATIONS

Gifts are of **GOD**, the Merciful and Kind, who out of His mere Goodness bestows them in various ways through the holy Spirit of **WISDOM** upon His own—that is, either mediately <note>through secondary means or teachers</note> or immediately <note>direct divine revelation</note>—according to the time and place (following what He sees will contribute to the glory of His divine name, and benefit those people and their neighbors to whom He distributes or gives the gift). Nor does **GOD** give everything to one person; rather, the better, more secret, certain, and select things are communicated to the "sons of Doctrine"—that is, the more faithful and those endowed with the required skill—and to certain chosen ones (who are few), as is fitting. Wherefore the Lily <note>A reference to a specific alchemical or hermetic text, possibly the 'Lilium de Spinis' or a similar work</note>, speaking of the **Philosopher's Stone** <note>original: "Lapide Philm."</note>, says: *If **GOD** knew a faithful mind in a man, He would surely reveal the truth to him.*

<margin>fear of god</margin>
<margin>binary</margin>
<margin>ternary</margin>
<margin>divine unity</margin>
<margin>by rejecting so that the binary and ternary, through the quaternary, may provide access to the simplicity of the monad, then you will find the kingdom of god and his justice, provided you ascend through the ladder of union and descend through the ten steps of knowledge</margin>

Be therefore in the **Fear of GOD** (clothed in the **TEN** Christian-Cabalistic garments <note>An allusion to the ten Sephirot or divine attributes in Christian Kabbalah</note> noted in the second figure of this *Amphitheater*) by totally rejecting the **Binary** and the **Ternary**, and reducing them through the **Quaternary** to the simplicity of the **Monad** <note>In this mystical mathematics, the "Binary" represents division or the fall; the "Ternary" represents the world of matter; the "Quaternary" is the sacred four (the name of God); and the "Monad" is the ultimate Divine Unity.</note>, according to the strengths granted by the Divine. Seeking the **Kingdom of GOD** and His Justice with your whole heart, whole soul, whole strength, and whole mind—or at least studying to seek it **Theosophically** <note>Seeking wisdom through divine illumination rather than just human reason.</note>—**JEHOVAH** does not reject your will: because in good things (by the instinct of the Best), it is enough to have willed well. *It is something to advance this far, even if it is not given to go further:* and *though the strength is lacking, yet the will is to be praised.* **Obedience pleases God well** <note>original German: "Gott gefält der gehorsam wol."</note>. Nor is **GOD** accustomed, as St. Paul testifies, to extinguish the glowing wick <note>original: "ellychnium candens," an image of God's mercy toward the weak in faith.</note>. If your aim is the glory of **GOD**, and "fie!" to the devil; and if it will benefit you and your neighbor (for there is a reason *why*, *to whom*, *when*, and *how much*), you will happily obtain what you seek from **JEHOVAH** by **Praying and Working** <note>original: "Orando & Laborando," the classic alchemical and monastic motto.</note>, ascending through the **Ladder of Conjunction and Union**, as well as descending through the **Ten Steps of Knowledge**. Indeed, you will be able to ascend to the knowledge of **ALL THINGS** that truly exist, whether by sense, science, or faith, from the bottom to the summit. 

<margin>principles</margin>

For the **LORD** will fulfill (nothing is more certain) your desire, you who fear Him, *Psalm 145:19*, see also verses 169 and 334. Therefore, let all doubt (a concept of the devil within you) depart from you: laboring wisely, believe **GOD** and in **GOD** with firm confidence; by not wavering in faith, you will find what you seek; it will be given to you; you will receive it; it will be done. O, the beast of unbelief! Pray to **GOD** that He may increase your faith. Faith is the Gift of **GOD**. *Do not take this from me, I beseech you, Lord!*

| **2** [manicule] And to receive the **LEARNING** <note>original: "ERUDITIONEM"</note> of **DOCTRINE**, **JUSTICE**, and **JUDGMENT** and **EQUITY**: | In the same place verse 3. | To receive the **LEARNING** of **INTELLIGENCE**, **JUSTICE**, and **JUDGMENT** and **RECTITUDES**: | **2** |

**And to receive**] Learning, which happens by Divine providence, must be embraced with great skill and a heavenly, holy desire. Also to be noted here is learned **Intelligence**; not that common, vulgar kind obvious to anyone, but that which tastes of heavenly learning—Theological, macrocosmic, and microcosmic <note>Relating to the "Great World" (the universe) and the "Little World" (the human being).</note>. This He distributes into **Justice**, which concerns the soul of man; into **Judgment**, which concerns the body; and into **Rectitude**, which shapes the spirit, morals, and the duty and vocation of each person: so that one may act holily in divine matters, justly in human matters, and rightly in one's own affairs, toward God, men, and oneself.

<meta>This page continues the "Interpretations" of the Prologue to the Proverbs of Solomon. It follows the previous page’s discussion on how God distributes wisdom and now begins to categorize the specific "steps" or "degrees" of knowledge, focusing on verses 4, 5, and 6 of the first chapter of Proverbs.</meta>

5

THE FIRST STEPS.

<margin>3</margin>
| | | |
| :--- | :---: | :--- |
| ☞ That subtlety may be given to the little ones, | **Verse 4.** | To give craftiness to the simple, |
| **KNOWLEDGE** and **UNDERSTANDING** to the youth. | | to the child **KNOWLEDGE** and **INTELLIGENCE** ☞ **REFLECTION**. |

**That it may be given to the little ones**] He calls "little ones" here (just as in verse 39) the simple, those who are unable to free themselves by their own counsels, and therefore look for help from the **LORD** and from the **WISDOM OF GOD**, their Helper; they are those who are not "wise in their own eyes" (Proverbs 3:7), as are the "wise of this world" (Romans 12:16). For from these latter, **GOD** hides His Wisdom—for which reason our Savior gives thanks to His heavenly Father in Matthew 11:25: *You have revealed these things,* He says, *to little ones.* <note>original: "Paruulis... reuelaſti hæc."</note> **Subtlety**] Subtlety here signifies circumspection and caution, so that we are not captured and led astray by the deceits of the world; but rather that we may be "wise as serpents, and simple as doves" (Matthew 10:16). That is (just as Saint Paul interprets in Romans 16:19), "wise in what is good, and simple in what is evil." <note>original: "ſapientes in bono, ſimplices in malo."</note> Understand therefore, O little ones, Subtlety, and you foolish ones, take notice. **Knowledge, etc.**] Knowledge and reflection are joined here so that we may learn to meditate, and by meditating to investigate knowledge, and by investigating to pray to **GOD**, and by praying to labor.

6 INTERPRETATIONS

It is read that the Queen of Sheba tested Solomon with such riddles. Joseph the Patriarch and the Royal Prophet David were divinely taught in these; the Prophets and the *Revelation* of John contain many such things. The Egyptians were famous for these, as they hid their mysteries in hieroglyphic signs. From this source come those mystical images with which the Magi, through admirable skill, depicted Divine, Theological, Political, and Natural Mysteries, as well as the hidden nature of things. From here also come those Hermetic Emerald Tablets <note>The *Tabula Smaragdina*, a foundational text of Hermeticism and alchemy, said to contain the secret of the "primary matter" and its transmutations.</note>, enigmas, and the famous pictures of the **Philosopher’s Stone**. Learn here (you who thirst for the nectar of truth from the wrappings of the Wise) the way and method of arriving at the understanding of enigmas, parables, allegories, and the mystical speeches of the ancient Sages in matters Cabalistic, Magical, and Chemical—in **ALL** things. *If you take **WISDOM** as your sister, and **PRUDENCE** as your friend (as it says in verse 106/Proverbs 7:4), you will understand and learn **ALL** things theosophically.* **Interpretation.**] A "measure," as the Hebrews say, and the "weight of the word." To this belongs the **Gematria** <note>original: "Gimetria"; a Kabbalistic method of interpreting Hebrew words by calculating their numerical value.</note> of the Kabbalists; **Notarikon** <note>original: "Teuos rasche"; shorthand or acronyms where each letter of a word stands for another word.</note>; and **Temurah** <note>original: "Neoteriken"; likely referring to the rearrangement of letters.</note>. Or, as John Dee of London <note>An influential Elizabethan mathematician, astronomer, and occultist.</note> expresses it in his *Aphorisms* to the Parisians and in his *Preface to King Maximilian* prefixed to the *Hieroglyphic Monad*: **Geometry, Notarikon, and Tzyruph.** And indeed, he calls this "Real Kabbalah" (or the **living** <note>original: ζῶντα (*zōnta*)</note> kind) from its signature; while the common kind he calls "Grammatical Kabbalah" (or the **spoken** <note>original: λεγομένην (*legomenēn*)</note> kind), which relies on the well-known letters that can be written by man. At this point, it is pleasing to include the verses which, twenty-seven years ago, the most distinguished John Olearius <note>A German hymnwriter and academic at the University of Helmstedt (the "Julia" Academy).</note>—Doctor of Theology and Professor of the Hebrew Language in the Illustrious Julia Academy—wrote in praise of the Kabbalah to Paul of Prague:

**Very tender**] Even boys, the tenderly young, and youths, from their earliest age, are to be instructed and educated in the **DISCIPLINE OF TRUE WISDOM**, as the example and command of this passage clearly teach. 8 INTERPRETATIONS

[*I too am indeed a mortal man.* <note>Original Latin: "Sum quidem & Ego mortalis homo." A quote from the Book of Wisdom 7:1.</note>] Someone might say: why would **GOD** reveal His mysteries? Why would He communicate the secrets of Nature to me? To me? Who am I? Am I not a sinner, and for that reason mortal? And, consequently, unworthy of such great **GOODS** and **GIFTS** of **GOD**—that is, the infinite treasures of **ETERNAL WISDOM** mentioned in this Prologue. I confess indeed, and I respond to such objections, that I am unworthy, yet I am in need. Listen to the Wise King [Solomon], who, while not yet walking perfectly in the precepts of David his father (for he was still sacrificing in high places and offering incense), was nevertheless filled by **GOD** in a single night's dream with the Wisdom of all things above and below. 1 Kings 3 <note>Original: "3. Reg. 3." In older Latin Bibles, 1 Kings was often cited as 3 Kings.</note>. At the same time, he was filled with such prudence in managing affairs that no one emerged as his equal. He said: *I too am a mortal man, like all others,* etc. Such a man also (I continue) was Bezalel <note>The artisan commanded by God to build the Tabernacle (Exodus 31).</note>; nonetheless filled with the Spirit of **GOD**, with Wisdom, Understanding, and Knowledge in every work, for devising whatever could be crafted from gold and silver, bronze, marble, gems, and various types of wood. To him was given a companion, Oholiab; and in the heart of every skillful person, **WISDOM** was placed by the **LORD** so that they might do all that Moses commanded. Exodus 31:3. Such a man also was David, who although he had not studied letters, yet by the anointing of the Spirit of **GOD**, was transformed from a shepherd into a Prophet and a preeminent Teacher of Divine things. He so filled his Psalms with these things that all poets, however exquisite, fall far behind him. He was a sinner, a womanizer, a murderer; yet he did not lose the name of a just man as often as he rose again through repentance. Elijah, says James 5:17 (timely meeting the present objection), was a man **LIKE US** (the Apostle by no means exempting himself from the common lot), subject to the same passions: and he prayed with prayer that it might not rain upon the earth, and it did not rain for three years and six months. And again he prayed, and the heaven gave rain, and the earth gave its fruit. So says he. You might persist by objecting: *Friend, do not compare yourself to these; **GOD** used those singular instruments in a singular way for singular purposes. Considering their vocations and yours are different, you yourself will judge differently.* To this I respond, good man: there is something in what you say, and indeed it would have deterred me, had not so many and such great universal <note>The Latin "Catholicae" here refers to the original meaning of "universal" or "for all," rather than specifically the Roman Catholic Church.</note> vocations, invitations, admonitions, and exhortations of **WISDOM** herself and of the Wise Man stood in the way; indeed, even threats under the most grave penalty of Divine wrath, which recall me everywhere in this Prologue. Furthermore, the universal Promise of **ETERNAL TRUTH** stands in the way and revives me; inviting all, excluding no one, repeated so often and noted a little further on. In this one truthful source I trust more than in your deceptive wagon-load of doubts. Therefore, I will wisely follow **WISDOM** and the Wise Man who call to me, divinely stimulating me to experience Divine things. Why should I exclude myself, if I am not excluded by **GOD**? Again, someone might doubt, saying: *I am young, my hair has not yet turned gray.* I counter: **GOD** is no respecter of persons, etc. (see verses 38, 184, 299). Nor does a learned old age, pleasing to **GOD**, consist in the mere multitude of years, but, etc., as in verse 351. Let the youth of Joseph, David, Solomon, Daniel, Jeremiah, Timothy, etc., and of countless others (even in our own century) who are not foolish, but are possessors (by the grace of **GOD**) of the inexhaustible treasures of **WISDOM**, be a comfort and an example to you. The same answer applies to the objection regarding a lack or deficiency in various languages—namely, Hebrew, Greek, Latin, etc. For **GOD** is also accustomed to raise up

### THE FIRST STEPS. 9

There are wise men and Doctors among those who are skilled in only their one and only mother tongue. Countless examples are at hand from every nation. It is **JEHOVAH** who gives the mouth and **WISDOM**, as seen in Exodus 4:11, Matthew 10:19, Mark 13:11, and Luke 12:11–12. *The Spirit of the Lord spoke through me, said David; and his word was on my tongue.* <note>Original Latin: "Spiritus Domini locutus est per me... & sermo eius per linguam meã." From 2 Samuel 23:2.</note> Holy men of **GOD** spoke as they were inspired by the Holy Spirit. 2 Peter 1:21. There is, therefore, no reason why you should distrust the grace of **GOD**, whose mercy is from eternity to eternity upon those who fear Him. Psalm 103:17. Such flimsy excuses <note>Literally "bald" or "bare" excuses (calvae).</note> cannot protect your laziness and lack of faith. (See verses 216 and 324). Good **GOD**, how long a catalog could I recite from the ancients (even including the Pagans) of the inventors of Sciences and Arts, the majority of whom were unskilled in various languages; and in our own century, the restorers and cultivators of these arts—all of whom were divinely stirred and taught and led <term>theosophically</term> <note>Khunrath uses "theosophically" to mean "by the wisdom of God" rather than modern occult movements.</note>—if the law of the preface did not restrain my pen. 

All these men, I say, were mortals just as you, I, and we are; indeed, they were even sinners. We have the same **GOD** today whom they had then: we are the handiwork of the one and the same **ELOHIM** Creator (in whose image and likeness all were formed). We enjoy the ministry, consolation, defense, protection, and direction of our ways by the same good Spirits <note>Referring to angels.</note> whom they enjoyed, sent by **GOD**. We enjoy the same Nature in the same World. The same most true and universal **PROMISE** given to us of the one and the same **ETERNAL WISDOM**—which was incarnated in the fullness of time—is also given to others.

What, you will ask, is that Wisdom in which you glory so much, and in which you trust so much? I answer rightly: It is the **WISDOM** which you have heard—and will hear in this Prologue—was to be incarnated. This same incarnated Wisdom, which is **TRUTH** itself, says in John 14:12: *Amen, Amen, I say to you—that is, to all, everyone, each and every person—he who believes in me, the works that I do, he will also do, and greater than these will he do; because I go to the Father. And whatever you ask the Father in my name, this I will do, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son. If you ask me anything in my name* (verse 14), *I will do it.* 

In Matthew 17:19, the disciples came to **JESUS** in secret and said: *Why could we not cast out that demon?* **JESUS** said to them: **BECAUSE OF YOUR LACK OF FAITH.** (Truly, this is still the case today!) *For Amen, I say to you, if you have faith like a grain of mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, move from here to there, and it will move,* **AND NOTHING WILL BE IMPOSSIBLE FOR YOU.** *However, this kind does not go out except through prayer and fasting.* In Luke 17:6, the **LORD** said: *If you had faith like a mustard seed, you would say to this mulberry tree: be uprooted and transplanted into the sea, and it would obey you.*

There you have it. Let us therefore cry out with the disciples of **CHRIST** (from the same chapter, verse 5): **O LORD, increase our faith.** If only you, who have taken the name of Christ, would learn through <term>theosophical exercise</term> <note>Khunrath's term for a meditative and practical spiritual practice aimed at attaining divine knowledge.</note> to ask the Father in the name of **JESUS CHRIST CRUCIFIED** and to **BELIEVE**, you would be able to do **ALL THINGS**. 

You persist further, O doubter, saying: Christ said these things only to the Apostles, just like that passage in Mark 16:17: *These signs will follow those who believe in me: in my name they will cast out demons, etc.* Therefore, they do not apply universally to all ministers of the Catholic <note>Here used in its original sense of "universal," rather than specifically Roman Catholic.</note> Church (let alone all Christians), nor to every time or place. I ask you, my lord, was this not also said to the Apostles? *Receive the Holy Spirit; whose sins you forgive, they are forgiven them; and whose sins you retain, they are retained.* John 20:22. And: *Go into the whole world and preach the Gospel to every creature. He who believes and is baptized...*

## Interpretations

If he was baptized, etc. (Mark 16:15). Especially so. If therefore, those words apply only to the Apostles, why not these? If the former exclude you, why do the latter (as you say) include you? Show me a separating command. If promises about the power of faith are not Catholic, why do you use them consolingly in sermons to everyone? But if they are, why do you (I won't say it harshly) fabricate? O perverse minds! Chapter 11 of the Epistle to the Hebrews is with me against you. I fear if the teacher of all Christians were to return, he would especially reproach you for your unbelief and hardness of heart because you have not believed those things which (convicted by the testimony of your conscience to the truth) you know he also said to you. Therefore, let no one despair of attaining the good things and gifts of Eternal Wisdom in a Theo-Sophic manner. The hand of the Lord is not shortened for all who invoke him in faith and truth. I commend to you the story of the healing through faith in Acts 3. Now, my brother, contemplate with your eyes and mind this whole Amphitheater of ours; it will teach you to find the Light of All Truth in eternal light. But the spectator must be illuminated by the spirit of Wisdom if he wants to reach the center. [Marginal Note: note] Otherwise, these things which are Divinely revealed by us Theosophically will be night. I add this: It is blasphemous for the Church to want to excuse its original laziness (verse 93) and un-Christian diffidence in a gigantic way, [as if the church is] to be confirmed by miracles. We have a Catholic promise of Truth, given once for all time, Eternal, which does not fail for eternity. It is your unbelief (with Christ as my witness, Matthew 17:20) that hinders the wondrous Good Things and Gifts of God. The promise of God, the Best and Greatest, has always been, is, and will be constant, firm, and ratified, strengthened and confirmed by the seal of God (which is EMES [Marginal Note: אמש, Lucid Truth], the first figure of this Amphitheater). Just see to it that your malice and distrust do not lightly shake or hinder its operation and effect. Many theologians (so-called) babble historically from the pulpits about faith, who do not demonstrate the presence of even an atom of active power of faith in effect. These people deny (I am not speaking of good men) in their lives and deeds what they affirm with their mouths. I know that the contrary has been done by the Fathers, and within our memory by theologians not to be despised, you yourselves know it, and others know and will testify to it. You ought to perform and obtain wondrous and rare things through Faith, not for confirming a doctrine of Religion, which I know is sufficiently confirmed (even without your prompting), but (please note this) for the power of Faith (as befits a Believer, so-called from Faith) and the office of Charity in exercising Christian compassion towards a needy neighbor. Therefore, I would like no one to believe that those are truly Theologians, however old they may be, however endowed with contentious loquacity, who are defiled by any kind of vice, by pride, hypocrisy, avarice, hatred, envy, drunkenness, and often (under the guise of religion) luxury, neglecting the gift of active Faith and the light of the mind, and following animal affections. AXIOM: *As much as anyone receives of the Divine, so much also has he of Faith; as much faith, so much wondrous power.* I understand faith not as that dead faith of James 2 (which is no more Faith than the devil is Holy, or a dead man is a man), but a living and active faith, as is described in 2 Peter 1. SUMMARY: Believe Christianly; live Theo-Sophically; fasting, Pray in Spirit and Truth, according to the Laws and Doctrine of this Amphitheater. I call God as my witness that, by wisely collaborating, what you ask of Jehovah Christianly (for the honor of himself, the needy neighbor, and your own honest utility, and to flee the devil) will be done. See verse 335. It is similar for all propagated from Adam, the first formed, who ate the apple.

# THE FIRST STAGE. 11

...brought forth as a child of the earth, under the same condition and Law as all others. This is a famous medieval Latin proverb reminding the reader that death is the great equalizer, treating the king's staff and the peasant's tool the same.</note>

*The path of death is the same for all, yet the manner*
*Of life’s departure is not one for every person.*
Ponder therefore, my brother, how this life is more fleeting than smoke, more empty than a shadow. Indeed, the days of our life flee like a shadow. 1 Chronicles 29:15; Job 8:9 and 14:2; Psalm 109:23 and 144:4; Ecclesiastes 7:1; Wisdom 2:5 and 5:9. They vanish like smoke. Psalm 102:4. They pass more quickly than a weaver’s shuttle cuts the thread. Job 7:6. They are faster than a runner. Job 9:25. They pass away like a spider’s web. <note>original: "meditantur, sicut aranea" — a reference to the fragile and fleeting nature of life, often compared to the breath or a spider's web in the Vulgate.</note> Psalm 90:9. All flesh is grass, and all its glory is like the flower of the field, blooming in the morning and falling in the evening. Isaiah 40:6-7; Job 14:2; Psalm 90:4-6; Ecclesiastes 14:18.

Considering this fragility of human life on one hand, and the infinite greatness of the Divine Majesty on the other, the Royal Prophet <note>King David, traditional author of the Psalms.</note> is seized with wonder and, as if astonished, breaks out in this voice: *What is man, that you are mindful of him?* Psalm 8:5. This same realization even forced tears from Xerxes, that strenuous and most powerful King, when he once looked down from a high and lofty place upon an infinite multitude of men and an innumerable army; he wept because not one of those he then beheld would be alive a hundred years later. <note>This is a famous story from Herodotus: the Persian King Xerxes the Great wept while reviewing his troops at the Hellespont, overwhelmed by the thought of mortality.</note> Therefore, compensate for this brevity of life with goodness and integrity, you who profess to be a Christian; consider not how long you live, but how well. And since nothing is more certain than death, yet nothing more uncertain than the hour of death, learn to die well by living holily in the fear of God.

18 INTERPRETATIONS

*The holy gods willed that the Teacher should hold*
*the place of a Parent.* <note>original: "Dii Præceptorem sancti voluêre Parentis Esse loco." This verse emphasizes the spiritual kinship between a student and their mentor, a common theme in both classical philosophy and alchemy.</note>

Alexander the Great is worthy of praise for saying excellently that he owed no less to his Teacher, Aristotle, than to his Father: for from his Father he had received the beginning of life, but from his Teacher the beginning of *living well*. <note>Alexander the Great (356–323 BCE) was famously tutored by the philosopher Aristotle. This anecdote was frequently used to argue that while parents provide physical life, teachers provide the moral and intellectual framework for a virtuous life.</note> Yet all of this depends upon the will of **GOD**. For it is not a matter of human will or of one running by their own power, but of the mercy (and the preceding grace) of **GOD**. <note>A reference to Romans 9:16, implying that even the best education requires divine favor to bear fruit.</note> To will, says Paul in Romans 9:16 and 7:18, is present within me; but I find no way to perfect what is good. (Therefore, there is a need for **GOD** as a co-worker.) <note>The author uses the concept of "co-working" or synergy to explain that the alchemist or seeker must work in tandem with divine influence.</note> And a little later in verse 22: "For I delight in the Law of **GOD** according to the inward man; but I see another law in my members, warring against the Law of my Mind, and bringing me into captivity to the Law of sin which is in my members." (Therefore, there is a need for **GOD** who brings [the work] to perfection.) Thus **GOD** has worked together [with humanity] from the beginning of time, as noted in Ecclesiasticus 51:11. Thus Christ worked together with the Apostles, who were sent into the whole world to preach the Gospel to every creature, and...

<summary>This page explores the relationship between human effort, the guidance of a teacher, and the essential requirement of divine grace. [Commentary 46]
**Now**] After you have heard who, of what sort, and how great I, WISDOM, am. **Who keep my ways**] This is to say, those who preserve or perform my commandments. You, says Christ—the incarnate WISDOM—in John 15:14: *You are my friends, if you DO those things which I command you.* And in the same book, chapter 13, verse 17: *You will be blessed, if you DO them.* Luke 8:21: *My mother and my brothers are these, who hear the word of GOD and DO it.* To do what the WISDOM of GOD has commanded is to walk in Her ways. Therefore, let him who wishes to acquire life amend his life, so that he may be clothed with life. Christ is the **Archetype** <note>The original model or pattern upon which all others are based</note>; he who knows Him, clothes himself in Him and imitates Him, is Wise, Blessed, and truly Christian. It must be noted: Although while we remain in this skin <note>original: "in cute hac hæremus"—a metaphor for the mortal body</note> it is necessary for us to be and live in the World, we must nevertheless flee daily and forsake the unclean world. How so? If, I say, in heart, words, and deeds, we do not cling to worldly impurities—that is, if we do not live in a worldly manner with the unclean world—then we are clothed in Christ and we imitate the **Archetype** through a **Theo-Sophic** <term>Theo-Sophic<gloss>Divinely wise; from the Greek 'Theos' (God) and 'Sophia' (Wisdom)</gloss></term> life. This is to draw near to GOD. He who has drawn near is enlightened, joined, and united. It is necessary for him who desires the fellowship of good spirits, more sublime contemplations, and a **DEIFYING** union, to become spiritual, good, and sublime in mind within the Spirit of the Best and Greatest [God]. For the conjunction and union occurs between like things, not unlike things. To lose oneself thus in the worldly circumference is to find oneself in the Center—that is, in GOD—and to find GOD within oneself. See verse 132. By this path of WISDOM, you withdraw from the world with Christ, even though you live and move daily in the World, even in the midst of those living worldlily: You live not worldlily, but Theosophically in and with Christ. *Better is WISDOM, etc.* <note>original: "Melior est SAPIENTIA, &c."</note>] For it is the source of all Good, just as we are taught here and there in this Prologue by the Wise Man. See verses 45 and 327. And certainly Divine **WISDOM** excels all physical might: for by a single serious and pious prayer, great power is often broken. Thus Moses, with hands raised, broke the power of Amalek, Exodus 14:11 <note>The text cites Exodus 14:11, but the account of Moses raising his hands to defeat Amalek is found in Exodus 17:11.</note>. Jehoshaphat, with a single hymn, broke the strength of the sons of Ammon and Moab, and scattered their army, 2 Chronicles 20:22. How often did David break the ferocity of Saul and other enemies with his hymns? Those who understand the hidden Nature of things can produce many such proofs, which the common people regard as miracles. History also testifies that many heroes were aided by natural strengths. But how often is victory or some cause won, or a people saved, through distinguished prudence? Was not Egypt saved by the Wisdom of Joseph? Persia by Daniel’s? The Israelite people by Moses’? In these instances, Wisdom was certainly better than strength.

**Against the LORD]** Since all true Wisdom is from GOD; against GOD, true Wisdom cannot fight. The WISDOM OF GOD is the Light, which no human philosophy can obscure; it is more lucid than all human and serpentine cunning: therefore it will penetrate, break through, and obtain the palm of victory against all sophistry. When the hour and day of true Wisdom dawns, all the masks of shadowy philosophy will vanish. Just as, when the Sun of Justice, Jesus Christ, arose, all the shadows and masks of profane religions vanished; and even now the darkness of false religions strives in vain to extinguish that shining Sun; (For what GOD has decreed cannot be changed by men.) <meta>This page continues the discussion of the "Steps" of spiritual or intellectual progress, specifically the Second Step. It moves from general principles of wisdom to observing the inherent intelligence and "sparks" of divine reason found within the animal kingdom.</meta>

OF THE SECOND STEP. 39

In the case of Adamantius, the most charming little dog of Julius Caesar Scaliger <note>Julius Caesar Scaliger (1484–1558) was a famous Italian scholar and physician; he wrote a moving epitaph for his beloved dog, Adamantius.</note>, his tomb—found in the first part of his master's poems—teaches us this. Nor are examples of others lacking, found almost everywhere. The ELEPHANT, the largest of land animals, is docile, mild, prudent, strong in memory, and "loving of mankind" <note>original: "φιλάνθρωπον" (philanthrōpon)</note>, according to Pliny in Book 8 of his *Natural History*, and Justus Lipsius <note>A famous Flemish humanist scholar.</note> in his *Letters*, as is also proven by modern experience. For eye-witnesses and trustworthy sources know what proofs of greatness of soul <note>The term "magnanimitas" suggests a noble or courageous spirit.</note> elephants have shown in Antwerp, Lisbon, and Vienna in our own time. The LARK <note>The Latin name is *Alauda*.</note> has its name among the learned from "praise" <note>original: "à laude"</note>, because it praises GOD so wonderfully and gives Him thanks for His gifts and good things; it has even been observed seven times that she flies into the heights and then lets herself down before taking a single grain from the earth for food. Is this not a rational thing—to praise GOD and give Him thanks? In these matters, they are far wiser than many inhuman men. Who taught the swallow to build such a skillful home for herself? "Four things," says Agur, the son of Jakeh (Proverbs 30:24, etc.), "are the smallest of the earth, and yet they are wiser than the wise: The ants, a people not strong, yet they prepare their food in the harvest; the rock badger <note>original: "lepusculus," literally "little hare," but referring to the *hyrax* or rock badger mentioned in Proverbs.</note>, a feeble folk, yet they make their houses in the rocks; the locust has no king, yet they all go forth in ranks; the lizard <note>original: "stellio," a spotted gecko or newt.</note> grasps with its hands, and dwells in the palaces of kings."

A great field is opened here for discussing the traces of Wisdom and Prudence in animals; however, let these few examples suffice for the present in place of many. I will add this: Plutarch felt that these things called unreasoning animals <note>original: "ζῶα ἄλογα" (zōa aloga)</note> are actually rational <note>original: "λογικὰ" (logika)</note>—that is, endowed with reason. (He might have said that if they do not possess it in full, they at least have certain sparks or atoms of reason and virtues). This is also what Lactantius <note>An early Christian author (c. 250–325 AD) often called the "Christian Cicero."</note> established, and in our time William d'Oncieu <note>original: "Guilielmus Oniacus," likely referring to the French jurist and author of "The Mysteries of Numbers."</note> defended in a specific writing on the mysteries of numbers. And all these (in my judgment as well) felt correctly: for while a spark of Divine Wisdom shines in all animals—whether of the land, the water, or the air—they are not entirely irrational, but are only lower than humans in their degree of prudence. In humans, Wisdom shines back far more abundantly. I fear that if some animals were granted the benefit of a tongue by the Creator (and not all men are equally wise or prudent), they might in some way satisfy those who cry out against this idea. The lack of spoken language will be made up for by the "language" of their works and deeds. Let the judgment rest with those who are experienced. The "groaning of the creation" in Romans 8:22 is not without meaning. You might object using that verse from the Psalmist: "In whom there is no understanding." <note>Psalm 32:9.</note> That is surely a weak objection. Is not the same thing often said of violent, angry, and fierce men, who are otherwise not lacking in reason? GOD is wonderful in His works; the entire universe speaks, confesses, and professes His Goodness, Omnipotence, and Wisdom (both specifically and universally)—if only there were those who would observe GOD speaking in the manner of the macrocosm <note>The "Great World" or the universe.</note> and understand Him.

SECOND STEP. 47

See to it that no one deceives you through **Philosophy** and empty deceit, according to the tradition of men, according to the elements of the world, and not according to Christ. <note>original Latin: "Videte, ne quis vos decipiat..." from Colossians 2:8.</note> That is, through a philosophy that lacks the **breath of GOD** and Divine enlightenment: relying on its own fantastical and worldly prudence, not on the light of truth in the Books of Holy Scripture, Nature, and Conscience, which are divinely written, handed down, and revealed.

*He who speaks perverse things*] In whatever field of knowledge you wish. Be it the Devil himself, or one perverse in law, a bad physician, a false scientist, a sophist, or any other who substitutes falsehoods for the right way under a disguised appearance of truth. Indeed, in every kind of state (about which every lover of Justice complains), such people everywhere hold the rudders of affairs today, so that among the Wise, it is almost entirely unsafe in this age to purely profess the Doctrine of **WISDOM**. So much has the smoke of malice grown strong! For if there are any (born of the Gods) <note>A classical idiom for people of noble spirit or divine inspiration.</note> who dedicate themselves entirely to **TRUTH**, they are called insane, ignorant, irreligious, and sometimes heretics; they are held in hatred, and even capital danger <note>original: "periculum capitale" — the threat of the death penalty or loss of legal status.</note> is decreed against them; they are afflicted with insults, and often deprived of the use of this light <note>A metaphor meaning they are either blinded, imprisoned, or killed.</note>. These are the rewards for lovers of **WISDOM** in this unclean world; **WISDOM** incarnate, our head, was itself injuriously affected by these things; let us, the members, bear similar things patiently. For it is the highest happiness to suffer from the worst for the sake of the Best. O the times! O the customs! <note>original: "O tempora! ô mores!" — a famous exclamation by the Roman orator Cicero against the corruption of his age.</note> May **GOD** give those people a rope and an end. <note>original: "funem & finem" — a sharp pun suggesting that the wicked should be brought to an end, perhaps by hanging.</note> Amen, says every lover of Theo-Philosophy.

<margin>
Capital danger is often decreed against those who profess the doctrine of Wisdom, because fools everywhere hold the rudders of the world today.

For as the proverb of P. Clodius and Varro says, truth is lost through too much arguing.

48 INTERPRETATIONS

**When they have done evil**] This refers to those most fraudulent people who have cunningly substituted and defended the false for the true, the unjust for the fair, and the impious for the lawful. Among such people, Law and Justice, Truth and Conscience, are nothing but a public commodity and an empty seeking of glory <note>original: "gloriæ aucupium" — literally "bird-catching for glory," a classical idiom for seeking hollow fame.</note> for the sake of the unlearned and profane masses, who value little based on truth but much based on mere opinion. May those perish who turn white into black. **In the worst things**] Woe to them: because they commit a sin against Conscience, which will not easily be forgiven.

**From the strange woman**] Here the Wise Man does not simply treat carnal fornication <note>sexual immorality</note>, but also that of the senses, reason, and mind, just as appears in verse 108. For just as evil conversations corrupt good morals, so do false dogmas <note>established beliefs or teachings</note> corrupt good minds. Worldly wisdom—foxy, puffed up, proud, contentiously argumentative, bombastic, blathering sounds without meaning through a chatter of empty words, and through dialectical tricks (I distinguish, dear Reader, the true use of logic from its abuse) through the winding paths of sophisms, stretching the nets of seduction—that is that enticing, smooth, and "strange" woman (Proverbs 7), the outsider, foolish and loud, who diabolically sells herself to fools under the most false title of "TRUE WISDOM." 

Yet, according to Paul, there is no truer foolishness before GOD than earthly wisdom; it must be unlearned by him who truly desires to be wise. In matters of Philosophy, listen to the philosopher Ludovicus Vives <note>Juan Luis Vives (1493–1540), a Spanish humanist and critic of scholasticism</note> (who should be believed as a craftsman in his own art), an old man strong in doctrine and experience. He says: "Those things which in my youth, with a high brow, I thought were treasures in Philosophy, now that I have changed and am an old man, I see are hardly better than dung, and were only delays to a pious life and necessary studies."

Thus he spoke. Also the Holy Fathers—Jerome, Ambrose, Augustine, Cyprian, Hilary, Basil, Cyril, Tertullian, Bernard, Prudentius, Isidore, and many other pious and learned men (of whom I could provide a long catalog if time and place allowed, their writings testifying to this abundantly)—deeply regretted the effort they spent in handling secular philosophy, which is always argumentative, pagan, and earthly. After many labors exhausted in it, they all finally agree that it is a plague to truth, to solid knowledge, to the Law of GOD, and to the Religion of Christ.
